issues.title: Please clarify the "native" authentication method
issues.author: mimi89999
issues.body:
Hello,

I noticed that the example JSON config file contains the `native` value in the `authentication` section. The meaning of that value however is not explained anywhere in the spec.

issues.title: Handling of multiple SRV records
issues.author: mimi89999
issues.body:
Hello,

The spec states that:
> The DNS server returns a DNS SRV record with the hostname of the HTTPS server where the PACC config file can be found:

However, it doesn't specify how the client should behave when multiple SRV records are returned. Should such a configuration be considered invalid? Can it use any value? Should it try all?

issues.title: SRV record from MX mentions EMAILDOMAIN
issues.author: mimi89999
issues.body:
Hello,

The section `3.2.3. DNS SRV query` mentions: `DNS SRV _paccmx._https.%EMAILDOMAIN%.`

I believe that there should be `%MXSERVER%` instead.

issues.title: Consider adding a section on https certificate validation
issues.author: mimi89999
issues.body:
Hello,

I noticed that the spec has a section on TLS certificate validation for the mail servers, but doesn't mention it for PACC retrieval. It's kind of obvious that the certificate must be validated, but I think that it might still make sense to mention it.

issues.title: Please add rationale for allowing users to accept invalid certificates
issues.author: mimi89999
issues.body:
The spec states that:

> If not, or if the TLS certificate is otherwise invalid, the client MUST either disconnect or MAY warn the user of the dangers and ask for user confirmation.

I think that an additional explanation of the reason for allowing the user to accept invalid certificates would be very useful. Do you want to support misconfigured servers? Abandoned servers with expired certificates? Servers that use self signed certificates or certificates signed by a corporate CA? In the latter case, it would be better to allow specifying the certificate hash in the PACC config instead of having the user manually verify the certificate hash.

If the spec does allow the user to accept an invalid certificate, there should be a parameter in the PACC file that does forbid that. Something like HSTS in HTTP.

issues.title: Doubts about relying on user verification
issues.author: mimi89999
issues.body:
The spec states that:
> Nonetheless, the result should be used with care. If such configs are used, the end user MUST explicitly confirm the config, particularly the resulting second-level domains. See section "User approval".

I doubt that it makes much sense to rely on user verification. This assumes that the user knows where a company mail is hosted and knows the exact domains or can easily find that information. That basically defies the whole point of having a mechanism like PACC or autoconfig. I also think that having users configuring their email clients over an untrusted connection isn't that rare. People might attempt to configure an email client on a mobile device when going for a trip or on holidays. If they end up doing it abroad, they will most likely be using a public WiFi network for that.
